title: Precise quantifiers
theme: Refined quantifiers (a few, a little, plenty of, hardly any, several, most)
goal: Student uses precise quantifiers for countable/uncountable nouns.
module_chunks: most + plural / most of + the + plural

units.title: Few vs a few (subtle)
units.grammar_focus: few/little (almost none) vs a few/a little (some)
units.real_life_context: You express positive (have some) vs negative (have almost none).

grammar.sentence: "I have _____ friends — we hang out often." (positive)
"I have _____ money — I can't help." (almost none)
"_____ people came to the party." (very few, negative)
"I have few friends and I feel happy." (Means almost none — feels off)
grammar.answer: I have a few friends and I feel happy.

grammar.sentence: "She has a little patience for delays." (Means some — but context suggests none)
grammar.answer: She has little patience for delays.

grammar.passage: I have few friends but a few good ones. She has little time but a little energy. We make it work.
grammar.question: How many good friends does the speaker have?
grammar.explanation: The text says "a few good ones".

units.title: Plenty of, hardly any
units.grammar_focus: plenty of (lots) vs hardly any (almost zero)

grammar.explanation: "Plenty of" = lots, abundance. With both countable and uncountable.

grammar.sentence: I have _____ books to read this summer.

grammar.explanation: "Hardly any visitors" — almost no one came.

grammar.passage: We have plenty of food but hardly any drinks. There's plenty of time but hardly any money.
grammar.question: What's scarce?
grammar.explanation: "Hardly any drinks" and "hardly any money" — both scarce.

listening_speaking.text: He has hardly any free time.

units.title: Several, most
units.real_life_context: You quantify with precision — several vs most.

grammar.sentence: I have _____ books on this topic.

grammar.explanation: "Most of the + plural" = majority of a specific group.

grammar.sentence: There are _____ ways to do this.

grammar.explanation: "Several" only with countable. For uncountable use "plenty of" or "a lot of".

grammar.passage: I have several books on history. Most of my friends like to read. Most people prefer fiction over non-fiction.
grammar.question: What do most people prefer?
grammar.explanation: The text says "Most people prefer fiction".

listening_speaking.text: I have several books on this topic.
There are several ways to do this.
